title: What does XLS-80 specify for Permissioned domains?
abstract: Sourced explanation of XLS-80 and its practical limits.
body:
According to XLS specifications, XLS-80 specifies credential-based permissioned domains whose owners choose accepted issuer and credential-type combinations. [1]

A domain represents a scoped membership definition on the ledger, not an internet hostname or a legal entity register. Accepted, unexpired credentials establish eligibility under that definition. Different domain owners can choose different issuers and types. Membership therefore means satisfying a particular ledger policy, not receiving a universal compliance approval. [1]

A published XLS document describes a design and its constraints; it is not by itself evidence that every network has enabled the corresponding amendment. Read the proposal status, dependencies and current network configuration together. Mainnet, Testnet and development networks can differ, and later fixes can change operational behavior. The source for XLS-80 was fetched directly from the public standards repository. [1][2]

The fetched specification records its status as Final. [1] Author interpretation: use XLS-80 as a specification reference and verify the actual network capability before promising it to a customer. Keep documented design, local tests and validated transactions separate when describing evidence. This article explains the standard rather than claiming a new live deployment. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
